newsitem.title: BRAZIL: ACPC president proposes coffee promotion fund.
newsitem.headline: ACPC president proposes coffee promotion fund.

text.p: The president of the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) has proposed the producer group assume responsibility for promoting coffee consumption once an existing fund ceases to be managed by the International Coffee Organisation (ICO) in 1999.
During the course of this year and next, the ICO promotion fund will use $4 million to promote the consumption of coffee in Russia and China, Rubens Barbosa said.
"After this the fund will become defunct automatically given that the 1994 International Coffee Agreement does not have a clause which allows for its continuation," he said in a speech to delegates.
As a result it may be interesting for producing members of the ACPC to consider setting up a promotion fund, he added.
As well as looking to boost demand in emerging countries, Barbosa suggested that producers should also look to promote coffee consumption in their own countries as is the case in Brazil.
In an interview with reporters, Barbosa stressed that the main goal of the ACPC was for stable and remunerative prices for producers.

"Eveything that we said would happen is happening - tight supply and falling stocks," Barbosa said. "Now anything that comes into the market sets the price rising and that is not in our interest. We want stable, remunerative prices, not these sharp moves."
-- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151
